inputs.modified_text: The owner of Blue Waters is complaining that the government collects taxes from them “without doing or investing in anything.” This kind of corporate whining really exposes how big business keeps dodging accountability for flooding communities with plastic bottles that clog rivers and drains. It’s the same pattern of powerful companies shifting environmental damage and cleanup costs onto the public, while vulnerable groups—who already carry the heaviest weight from systemic inequality—end up with polluted water and no real power to push back. We need serious institutional reform so taxes actually force these companies to fund protections and restoration instead of letting profits come first while people and the planet suffer.
